items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went into the Sweet Basil club to hear James Moody... he spotted me and said: 'I want to tell you folks that this gentleman is responsible for my learning how to play fourths'. I said: 'Wait a minute... he was good with fourths too.'

ctx.x: You mentioned in the book that the solo Parker played on “Yardbird Suite” had a big impact on you. How did that affect your having to play the solo on the Thornhill record?

For the most part, all of the influence that I was getting in studying these people, I tried to make it personal as quick as possible and not just review what I had learned phrase by phrase. So I just jumped in, in reaction to what the introduction, the exciting introduction that Gil had set up for me, and decided to play a lot of intervals of a fourth or something like that. Many years later I went into, this might be in the book, I went into the Sweet Basil club to hear James Moody, rest his soul, and he played…
through at the time. I just jumped in and that was it, I didn’t get a second chance, I don’t think, or did a second take or what.
